utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: We'll come to that date now. The document is addressed to lower and higher courts and public prosecutors. And if we go to the bottom of that page, it is addressed to Doboj, Teslic, Derventa, and Modrica. And if we go to page 2 of that document it appears to be -- the signature box has the name of Mr. Momcilo Mandic, minister of justice. If you look at the paragraph and if we go back to the top of the page in English --

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: No, no, go back to the top of page 2 but the top of the page. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Could you read the beginning of the paragraph right after the word "Modrica," Mr. Vidic. The paragraph that begins with: "Please submit ..."

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: "Please submit a list of all workers (by name) to this Ministry by 16 July 1992 and specify the president of the court, the judge, the public prosecutor, and the deputy prosecutor, the warden of the prison, as well as other workers with university education, training, VKV and KV, as well as the number of the Giro accounts into which we will pay wages. "Furthermore" --

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: You can stop there. We can see the rest. Mr. Vidic, here the request is to provide this information by 16th of July. And at the top of the letter, it says 13th of February. Would allow that there is an error in the date at the top of the document? You can scroll up in the B/C/S version at the top of the document.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: As I said, I don't remember this letter. And it says here who the addressees are. It says to higher court and lower and public prosecutor's offices, et cetera. It doesn't say that it should be sent to Doboj. As far as this date is concerned, I honestly don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And if you remember the prior document, it did refer to a circular of the Ministry of Justice with the same number. When you provided that information to the Ministry of Justice, do you remember a document coming to you ordering you or requesting this information, the list of staff members in your prison?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: I really don't remember. I didn't provide an answer just out of the blue. It was probably in response to the request by the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, we will have another witness who will -- who can authenticate this document. But at this time, I'm open, I'm in your hands. We can admit, unless there is an objection by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we do not object to this document being admitted, and we confirm that -- that obviously it's a typo, because it refers to the Serbian republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina and it's signed by Mr. Momcilo Mandic as minister of justice of -- of Serbian republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and we know that it is probably the 13th of July, 1992, instead of 13th of February. So we don't -- we do not object that this document be admitted at this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Then I seek to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P1307, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Vidic, in relation to your contacts with the Ministry of Justice, did you -- were in touch with any members of the ministry? And for the period of time, I'm talking about from the time that you were in charge of the prison.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: I had tried to get in touch with the minister. I called Pale and on one occasion, they gave me a number somewhere in Belgrade. I got in touch with the minister and -- but as soon as we started talking, the line was broken, and that was the last time that I spoke to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Did you make any other attempts to get in touch with members of the Ministry of Justice?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were attempts of that sort. When the presidents of the courts in Doboj and the prosecutor discussed among themselves about being obliged to do something and that they should get in touch with the ministry and seek support from some quarters, both economic and political, that we should have someone behind us. And that is when we reached an agreement, and I agreed to go to Pale on behalf of the prison, and the prosecution and another lady who was in charge of finances. And, of course, there was a driver with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: When did you go to Pale?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: I don't remember when it was exactly, but it could have been, let's say, between the 8th and the 15th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And just to be clear, which year are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And do you remember which building in Pale you went to?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: To Bistrica Hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And did you meet with anyone in Pale?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. But none of those with whom I had originally intended to meet. I met Mrs. Biljanja Brkic [phoen] who was working at the time at the Ministry of Justice.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: What was her role?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't know. But she definitely was not in the department for the execution of criminal sanctions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And did you have any discussions with her about the situation in Doboj?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Yes. I had to tell her about the purpose of my visit.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And could you explain to the Trial Chamber what you told her exactly. What was the purpose of your visit?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: The purpose of this visit was primarily to find someone who would provide either the money or the food for the prisoners. And also to find someone who would give us information and to give us some guidance, because the documents that we received with the prisoners were incomplete.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Could we display 65 ter 35 -- 3537, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And did you receive it in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And is this the -- your official appointment as warden of the prison in Doboj?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: May this be admitted, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P1308, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Could we display 65 ter 3071.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: What was the purpose of this decision? If you know.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: I -- no. It is obvious that this was typed as a kind of template for each institution. However, the truth is, that the Doboj district prison is the only penal and correctional facility that continued to operate while the other institutions were being in the process of being setting up. It was only the district prison in Doboj in 1992, at the beginning of war, already had on its premises the convicts, the persons who had already been sentenced, and other prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Was this document delivered to you at the time?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And, to your knowledge, were you told why this decision was issued? If the prison already existed at the time, why was this issued to you?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: No, I wasn't told. And I didn't even ask. I didn't think it was relevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And does -- if we can go to the second page, please. Who -- do we see that this document is signed by Dr. Radovan Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And that this document was to be entered in the Official Gazette of the Serbian People in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: May we admit this document, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P1309, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Could we please display on the screen 65 ter 3531.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Vidic, you told us that the warden of the prison was bound by -- bound to report to the Ministry of Justice. We have a document here of the 12th of December, 1992. Subject is: Information on the situation in Doboj district prison. First of all, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Is this your document?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: At the bottom of the first paragraph, paragraph headed: Information on the establishment, you provide a historic on the establishment of the prison and the last part of the sentence reads that: "... existing penal and correctional institutions ... including Doboj district prison, were taken over by and continued operating as organs of the state administration of Republika Srpska."

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Is that a reflection of the -- the decision we saw issued by Dr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now section -- paragraph 3: Information on detainees. It reads, as you were telling us, that on the 2nd of May there were 24 detainees in the prison, among whom 11 were in custody, 11 were imprisoned pending appeal, and two were convicted. If we go to the second page in English, we can keep it -- we can keep the B/C/S there. It continues and says that: "From 2nd of May, there were about 1.000 persons in and out of the prison." You wrote this document. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And what did you base this figure of 1.000 persons? What was it based on?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: It was based on these provisional documents that we ourselves set up and on the basis of the orders that we received from the police. However, although I say here 1.000 individuals, there were definitely people who came in two or three times, the same people.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I understand. Section 4 deals with the conditions of accommodation and living.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Demirdjian, could we ask what is meant by 1.000 persons in and out of the prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Vidic, you heard Judge Delvoie's question. What do we mean by 1000 persons in and out?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: That means they were admitted and released.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And at the time that you drafted this document, you say here that there were still 111 persons in the prison?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: With regards to section 4 of your report, it refers to the visit of International the Red Cross. Do you remember when the Red Cross visited the prison?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: I think it was in August or the beginning of September.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Earlier during your testimony today, you mentioned UNHCR. Did you mean that both organisations visited the prison, or was it one rather than the other?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: The International Red Cross visited the prison, while the UNHCR supplied the region with food. All the food aid that arrived in Doboj from this organisation was unloaded by convicts and uploaded again and transported to destination; whereas, we received food for our own prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And approximately when did the UNHCR provide this food?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: I -- I don't remember anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And if we look at the last page, please, in both English and B/C/S. Is that your signature, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, may that be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P1310, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours I'd like to now turn to the log-books of the prison. I don't know how much time I left before the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] We are about -- it's 11.58, we break at 12.05. Sorry. If you think it would be a more efficient use of time to take the break now and pick up afterwards, we could break five minutes early.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I think that would be fine because we are entering -- before we break, could I make sure that Your Honours have a binders of the registers?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: The way that I'm going to be proceeding is the following: Considering that these log-books are quite voluminous, we will be referring to documents in e-court, cross-referencing them with the log-books in front of you, so this is how I wish to proceed after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: May I continue, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Just before we continue, a matter for the transcript Mr. Zecevic brought to my attention. And at page 51, line 25, I was quoting from P1310, paragraph 3. At line 25, it reads 11 were in chain of custody. It was 11 were in custody. That's a typo in the transcript. We can see it from the document. At this stage could we display on the screen 65 ter 3079. And, Your Honours, in your binders this is tab 3. And if I could have the assistance of the usher, I have a binder for the witness as well. And if we could turn -- change to tab 3 for the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court what the document is?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: This is a register of detainees.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And on the cover page, it's a little bit erased, but it appears that we start with the year 1989 until 1994; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: If you turn to the next page --

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, Your Honours you will notice that because the ERN numbers do not appear properly on this document, we paginated them by hand. So we will follow the numbers. And another comment is that, to save resources, the interpreters, translators, translated only the names that were in Cyrillic. They didn't re-type the names that were in Latin letters, and we will have to do with what we have to go back and forth between the B/C/S and the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Vidic, I will ask you to turn to the detainee number 77, which is on page 16. In English, the pages are off by one page, so that would be page 17. Actually, it is page 16, I'm sorry. It is correct. Now, we see that this individual by the name of Rajko Kostasinovic [phoen] was detained on the 18th of April, 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And next detainee, number 78, is detained on the 21st of May, 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, first of all, who enters the details in this log-book?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Chief of the guard service.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And, as you said, this is the log-book for - I apologise - the detainees.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes. If you go to the next page, page 18, and as you go around these pages, do you recognise the handwritings? Because now we are in the month of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: From number 87 on, is my handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And if you turn the pages, can you tell us until when do we see your handwriting?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Up to and inclusive with number 122.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, this was not your -- this was not part of your regular functions; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Could you explain to the Court how it came that you had to enter those names in the log-book?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Mr. Slavuljica was already gone. The colleague who was supposed to stand in for the head of the guard service was away as well, and I think he returned only in August, and when he returned, he continued to make entries. And we, in the prison, employed only professionals. There were very few of us, and that's how it happened, that I also made entries in the book.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. Could you go to page 20 and look at detainees as of number 96.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Do you see the name of Mr. Senad Mesic?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, if you -- the row continues on page 21 for this individual's detention. Does it indicate which organ issued the order for imprisonment?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: It says: "Lower court."

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: In Doboj.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, this is one of those situations where I will ask to juggle between the screen and the log-book.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: If Your Honours have the page open at page 20, 21, I would ask at the meantime to display on the screen, 65 ter 3524.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, sir, this is a report we will see on the second page. On the first page is says, Case against Senad Mesic, Esad Hidic et al. If we can go to the second page, please, we see that this is issued by the public security station in Doboj on 18th of May. This is a criminal report, and the first individual there is Senad Mesic. Does the details in this report, his date of birth, and place of birth, connect with what is in the log-book as detainee number 96? Is this the same person?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, in the log-book, we see that the date for the detention is in parentheses, 17th of May, 1992. In the log-book at page 21. Do you see the date in parentheses?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And above that we see a few entries where we have a date, and below the date, we have another date in parentheses. Could you explain to the Court why do we have these two dates in some situations and what the parentheses mean?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: That's because in this -- in these provisional records we were keeping, when a person would be first brought in, we would note it down this way. Although in the documents of the prosecutor's office and the court, this date in brackets did not feature, but we noted it down just to have a rough estimate before we find out the exact information, because it's obvious that the court did not cover this time in which we knew, from our records, that the person was detained.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, the document from the public security station, Doboj, is the 18th of May, and the detention begins on the 17th of May. Could you explain to the Court how it is that the individual appears to be first detained and then this report comes the next day?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: I cannot explain that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: That's fine. We will have another witness to deal with this document. I will not go through all the names in this criminal report. But, for example, if you look at number 3, under the number of Murat Husakovic, do you see him also being included in your log-book at number 97?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, we will have another witness to authenticate this document. But for this time, can we just mark it for identification?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: What's the purpose if I may ask of -- what is it that you wish to show with the -- with these log-books?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: At this time -- well, perhaps if we can ask the witness -- not the log-book, Your Honour, I was just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: No, the register.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: The criminal report, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] The 65 ter 3524?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, that's the one that I wish to MFI at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Which, if I'm not wrong, is not on your list.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Where is my list?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may be heard on the subject. The Defence does not object if my learned friend wants to introduce this document through this witness. So it doesn't need to be MFI'd. It's a criminal complaint, and we don't see any problem with that being tendered as evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, just to answer Judge Delvoie's question, you are quite right; this document is in Doboj package to be tendered through the next witness. So I don't wish for it to be tendered, I apologise. I just wanted to display it to the witness. But you're quite right; it should have been on my list as a document to been shown to the witness. But, in any case, we have the person who drafted this criminal report who will be able to -- yes. So just for reference purposes, if it could be marked for identification for now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P1311, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, in response to Judge Harhoff's question as to the purpose of this criminal report, that is the reason why I wanted the witness to remove his headphones, it was to show the ethnicity of the people against who measures were taken in May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: May I move on?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Vidic, if we go back to the log-book to the detainee at number 96, does it show that this detainee was released on the 9th of March, 1993?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Yes. It says here in the log that he was transferred to the military investigative prison in Banja Luka, military remand prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. I will ask you to turn now to page 30 of the log-book and to look at detainees number 144 to 156. Do you see that page?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Can you read the name of the first individual in detention.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Miroslav Pijunovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And if go to the next page, page 32, so if you just flip the page, all the way down to number 156, the first name on that at page 151 do you see as Dario Slavuljica?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I'm being told that it's not on the screen. If we can go back to 65 -- 3079 on the screen, please. Mr. Pantelic, you should have a log-book as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but Mr. Pantelic was intervening on behalf of our clients because they don't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes. I'm waiting for it to be displayed on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes. The name at number 156, is it Zoran Sljuka?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, this group seems to have been detained as of the 17th of July, 1992. Do you remember the circumstances of the detention of this group?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: A bit. It was rather guess-work, from what I remember about the circumstances. And later there was media reporting about this group, and I simply don't want to make a mistake, if I tell you anything specific about what was happening at what time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And you said that these were reported in the media. How was this group known? Were they known by a certain name?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Could you provide that name?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: The Mice.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: While you have that page open, can we display on the screen 65 ter 859. Sir, do you see the document on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: It is a document issued by the Teslic Lower Court. Do you see the reference number? And can you tell us the reference number, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: It reads 33 in the transcript. Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: 33 or 35. It's a bit fudged.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I understand. And if you look at the log-book, back at the log-book, for entry number 144, Miroslav Pijunovic, do you see the number appear in your log-book?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Yes, 35.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And in order for you to detain these individuals in the prison, did you have to receive the decision from the Teslic Lower Court?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And do you remember receiving the document at that time?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And in relation to the person detained as number 151, Dario Slavuljica, did you remember seeing him later in that year?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: He later worked with us as a medical technician, but I can't tell you as of which date.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And -- very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Could I ask for the Teslic Lower Court's decision to be admitted. Again it is on the other list, Mr. Demirdjian.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I have it on this list as 859. It is pretty much the last document -- one of the last documents. You should see it as tab 62, perhaps, 65 ter 859.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Tab 62.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: If the tab numbers were sent, were they as well? Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: You're right. Sorry, my mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Sorry, could you assist me with where we are going with this process. Like, for instance, the last document, the order of court by which the particular person was -- was taken into the prison. Does it -- we have testimony of the process already from the witness who was on the stand --

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: -- that ordinarily a person would only be received into the prison on a warrant from the Court. I'm not sure about the utility of, for example, exhibiting the particular court order in respect of a particular witness. Is there a reason for that?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This document will be used with subsequent witnesses who can talk about the procedure that took place in relation to the document, the way it was drafted, the interviews with the detainees, and their subsequent release. At this stage the only evidence that this witness can provide is his angle, was that he received the court order and he detained the individual. That's as far as we can take it with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Even accepting that, to what end?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes. The issue in this case with relation to this group was that in relation to their activities in the municipality of Teslic, their arrest, their detention, and their release, and ultimately the lack of measures taken against this group.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And you -- you require for your case the documentary support for the evidence that you are going to be leading orally from the witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, to corroborate what he is saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, with we not object that this document be admitted on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Apart from that, what we're trying to understand is whether this procedure is in dispute.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No, it's not, as far as we are concerned. The only thing is, if I may be of assistance to Your Honours, this decision is not about the detention. This decision is initiation of the investigation against this group. So these people were already in detention. And by this decision the -- the court initiates the investigating proceedings to establish whether there is a foundation to -- to file the -- to proceed in the criminal trial with these people. So it is -- it is not disputed by us. It is just the completely different aspect that we are -- that we are saying it shows, not what -- what my learned friend is stating. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is clearly a matter in dispute between the parties. This is a -- the crimes committed by this group is charged -- they are charged in the indictment. This goes to prove the procedure that took place once this group was arrested, and, obviously in our indictment, we are claiming that there was a lack of measures taken against this group. And this is why we need to show what was the procedure that was actually taken and to show that we think that this is not the appropriate measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P1312, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I am finished with the log-book that we have in front of us, which was 65 ter 3079.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I do have one question, Mr. Vidic. Apart from this group, the Mice Group that we saw, apart from this group would it be fair to say that as of the month of May 1992, the majority of the detainees were non-Serb.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, since the witness recognises the log-book as belonging to the Doboj Central Prison, I would ask this document to be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: This log-book.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P1314 [sic], Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Could we display on the screen 65 ter 3570.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Vidic, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Well, I saw it when shown by the investigator. I remember it from that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. And this document is dated the 17th of July and drafted by the Doboj High Court. It is again in relation to the Mice Group that we were discussing earlier. I would like, in the English version, to turn to page 2. And in your language, sir, if you go to paragraph 4 which begins with: "Since the Doboj High Court has jurisdiction over the Serbian municipality of Teslic ..." Are you able to provide us any comments about this issue, the issue of jurisdiction over Teslic?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: District court had jurisdiction over the lower court in Teslic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And in this letter, the high court is proposing for the transfer of the detainees to the Doboj prison. And the next paragraph reads: "We shall transfer the said individuals at 1200 hours on the 18th of July, 1992, by our prison bus." Can you provide the Trial Chamber with your views on what happened?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: I can't remember who told me and who asked us to provide one of our buses, but I know that a bus went to Banja Luka and that these detainees had arrived in Doboj before and the bus went back empty.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm really sorry to interrupt, but there is -- there might be a problem. Maybe I'm missing. I believe the log-book, the previous document, was admitted and marked as P1314. But it should be 1313, I believe. Because the previous document was 1312 so ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Thank you. The document is, indeed, 1313. I was intending to correct the transcript next time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Vidic, can you see the signature block of this document at the bottom? Perhaps if it could be zoomed on that.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, the last name is a little bit smudged, but what is the title that will we see for the person who signs?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: It says here the President of the Higher Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: We can see the first name. Are you able to tell us who was the president of the high court at the time?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: In the earlier days, there was commissioner, Miroslav Lazarevic. And after that, for a while Goran Neskovic was president of the high court. Followed by Sava Lejkovic [phoen]. Which one occupied the position at what time, I couldn't say exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions on this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Could it be admitted, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P1314, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Could we now turn to tab 6 in your binders, Your Honours, and that's 65 ter 3076. And if the witness could --

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Vidic, if could you can go to tab 6 in your binder, please.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Which tab?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Number 6. Do you recognise this book?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: It should be in this book. These records should be in this book.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry. I was just asking you if you recognise the book?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: What was the purpose of recording names in this book?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: The purpose was for us to know who went out and who is supposed to come back to prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, this is a book that was kept in the prison?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And who was entering the data in this log-book?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: The duty officer at the prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: If you look at the first page, after you turn the cover, and you look at detainee number 2, what does this log-book tell us about his movements?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: It says that he had been taken to the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Who would take the detainee to the MUP?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: A MUP employee would come with an order for escorting this person, and, on the basis of that order, he would take him out.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Do you see his name repeated at number 6?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: At number 13?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: On the following page, do you see it repeated at 33 and 44?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And is it correct that each time, he is taken to the MUP?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: On -- on the page that starts with detainee number 31, we see next to detainee number 37, the name Lugonjic. Who -- do you know who Lugonjic is?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: I can't see the name of Lugonjic. I don't know who that person is anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. I will ask you to -- well, first of all, do you see the name? It's number 37, Hasan Omerasevic and if you continue along the line, you see under the comments, "Taken to work to the MUP." And you see "Lugonjic." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: But you're telling us you don't know that person.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, could you go to page 5, which starts with detainee number 118 -- I apologise, page 3. Page 3 which begins with detainee number 60. And go down to detainee number 82. Do you see the name at number 82?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Who was the person by the name of Karlo Grgic?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: He was the police station deputy commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And this was prior to the war?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Does this log-book show that he was taken out on the 12th of May and returned on the 15th of May?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And does it say that he was taken to the MUP for interview?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now I will ask you to go to page 6, entry number 147.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm sorry, Mr. Demirdjian.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I don't think you are right. I don't think you are right. I believe the -- the entry at 81 says, At 9.15. And then that "at" was copied afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: The "at" for the date, 15th of May, which is copied --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't think so. I think it's the 12th of May, and it says "at 9.15." And there's no date.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I was talking about, first of all, number 82.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] I know, but if it is -- if -- if this sign in 82, it copies the previous entry. And the previous entry, as I can see, says "at 9.15." So it might be the 12th of May he was taken at 9.00, the number 81, and returned at 9.15. That's -- that's what I -- what I noted.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Let's clarify this with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Vidic, detainee number 80, Nadja Seric, on what date was that person returned to the prison?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: It says here the 15th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Detainee number 81, Fadil Ahmic. On what date was he returned to the prison?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Apparently one cannot say precisely by looking at this. It is clear that he came back at quarter past 9.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, what does little sign mean? Or the date? Those quotation marks, or those little lines.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: That's why I'm saying, that one cannot say precisely. This sign, ditto, means that it is identical to the previous one. I think that Fadil was taken at 9.15, only the date was not recorded here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And the ditto, is it a ditto for the date that is above? What was the ditto used for?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: It's the handwriting of one and the same person. And I can only suppose that Fadil Ahmic was taken out on the 12th of May at 9.00 and that he was returned on the same day at quarter past 9.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, at what time was he taken out on the 12th of May?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And if you look at Karlo Grgic just below, on what day was he taken out?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: The 12th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Isn't there a ditto right there?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Yes, there is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And doesn't the ditto repeat the date above?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Wouldn't the same be replicated in the next column?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: But this is still open to interpretation, isn't it? Because if you go over the page, the column which seems to suggest date on which they returned are dates earlier than the 15th. So notwithstanding the dittos that appear from 81 going down, it appears, and perhaps this is something that the witness could explain, that the date 15/5 where it first appears seems sort of out of sync with the dates that follow it over the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Vidic, how would the ditto be used generally? What is it referring to?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: To put it simply there was no strict rule and there was no obligation to put the full date always or to use this sign ditto. It was left to the discretion of every person who kept these records. So I believe that you will find plenty of examples like this, both in this document and in other documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And, I mean, in order to clarify as much as possible now in-chief, I just suggest to go through other entries, which is above, and there is a pattern, there is a logic. For example, the same day and only the changes in the time, so maybe it's a typo there, or I don't know. I don't want to speculate, really. But we have a much stronger pattern above all these entries, which -- which is logical. I really don't want to -- to waste time, and I'm, again, sorry to interrupt my learned friend.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Just to clarify the matter, Mr. Vidic, it appears that, if we look at the chronological order, the dates above are the 10th, the 11th, and then there is a skip to the 15th. Could that be an error?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: It's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yeah, a mistake is possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I guess, the issue --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Sorry. There is -- there could be some logic now if you are -- if you are getting somebody out in the first column on the 12th, and all these dates in this column are sequential, if it doesn't come back but on the 15th and you have people going out on the 12th and on the 13th - next page --

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: -- then it is quite normal that the 15 comes before the -- the date of re-entry from the man who goes out on the 12th or on the 13th. So the fact that the 15th is here not sequentially in -- in this column, doesn't mean it's an error.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I guess the issue it whether the ditto signs refer to the information above or refer to the horizontal information that -- in the other column.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Vidic, you have something to add.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vidic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe this is obviously a mistake. Nadja was taken out on the 12th of May and was taken back on the 15th. If we look that the whole column beneath her name is identical. If you look at number 81 to 88, they all were taken out on the 12th. But it seems from here that they were all brought back on the 15th. But the next column, you see different purposes, loading goods, going to MUP, et cetera. To me, it tells me that this is a mistake in the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Vidic, can you turn to page 6 of the log-book and look at entry number 147. Do you see the name?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Is it the same name, Mr. Karlo Grgic? Now on this occasion --

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I apologise. On this occasion, where was he taken?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: To hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: From which day to which day?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: From the 16th to the 19th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Do you recall Mr. -- at the time, in 1992, these events when Mr. Grgic was taken to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: I remember that period, but who can possibly remember so many people, where they were taken to, and on what date. I only remember that there were people who were taken to hospital in that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And do you remember for what reason they were taken to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: They were taken because of the injuries that they had sustained.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Do you know where they sustained those injuries?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Well, I cannot say anything about that. Probably in prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: The last entry I want to refer to is on page 12. Detainees as of number 312. And 312 to 321. You see as of Bajro Huditi, all the way down to 321, Karlo Grgic, what is the first comment in the next column, 24th of May? What does it say?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Taken to work.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And right next to that in big letters what is written there?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Released.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Do you remember the circumstances of the release of this group?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, there are many other entries, but at this time, I will seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P1315, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And I would remind counsel that the three hours that were granted for this witness would be exhausted by 1.30 which is in 13 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I plan on finishing by that time, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, can we now go to --

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, before I continue, this was the document that was shown to the witness yesterday, if you remember we marked it for identification. The witness marked names with a red, with a cross. This is the same document. Now if we can have both versions admitted now that the witness has authenticated this document. The version marked by the previous witness and this unmarked version, as well. It was P1299, MFI.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I apologise. That -- I retract what I just said. It's another log-book. I will get to that one now. I apologise. It is it tab number 5. This is the one that I'm talking about now. 65 ter 3075. This is the one that was shown to the witness yesterday, but I will show him now the unmarked version.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, this is another log-book. Do you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Was this kept in the prison?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And who was in charge of entering names in this book?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: If it is a book, then that would be the head of the guard service.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And if you look through the pages of this book, what was the purpose of keeping this book, in comparison to the others?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: These are records that we established on our own. It is not statutory. So, if this was a book, this was taken by the head of the guard service. However, since I see that this is a makeshift book, this was being kept by the prison duty officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And does this book show the date when a detainee was detained and released?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: No more questions for this document. Could it be admitted, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, could we go to tab 4, please. And that is 65 ter --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could we have the exhibit number, please, first.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes. And Mr. Smith.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P1316, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And Mr. Smith has reminded me that now would be the time to admit the MFI from yesterday, 1299.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: We lift the MFI.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Right. 65 ter 2798, tab 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I would, just for the clarity of the record, and I will it assist everybody, if my learned friend can read the 65 ter number of 1299, which was MFI'd, and the -- and the document which was admitted as P1316, so we can have a clear distinction between the two. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes. Yesterday, the document which was marked as P1299 was 65 ter 10345. And today, it was 65 ter 3075. That was admitted as P1316.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Vidic, do you recognise this book?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Could you tell us what this book is.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: This is another log-book that we established. It was not prescribed by the rules and regulations. I would prefer to call it an index book. We tried to list all these names according to the alphabetical order. I don't remember exactly, but I don't think that this book was being kept until the end, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Just to clarify one matter that was raised yesterday, Mr. Vidic, can you go to page 25 in the B/C/S version, which is page 20 in the English version. Now, detainee number 12. Do you see his name?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: What is the -- what is the name, please?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Ilija Tipura.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Does it say that he was detained from the 4th of May until the 9th of September, 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And just very quickly, what was the ethnic background of Mr. Tipura?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: He was a Croat.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And what was the ethnic background of Mr. Grgic? I didn't ask you -- I didn't ask you earlier.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: A Croat.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Can I ask for this document to be admitted, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P1317, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Right. I have two topics to cover, and I will be finished, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Vidic, you told us that you had established some contact with members of the MUP in Doboj. Can you tell us who were your contacts at the MUP?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: That was Obren who was the chief of the police station. He was at the head of the criminal investigation department, or at least I think so. In the State Security Service, it was a man called Zivkovic, first name Dusan or Dusko. And finally, Marko Mihajlcic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Did you interact with them during the months of May, June, July 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Yes. Not often, but we did meet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: What was the gist of your conversations with -- first of all, you mentioned Obren, but his last name is not recorded. Can you give us his full name, please.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: His last name was Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And what was the gist of your conversation? What was the gist of your conversation with Mr. Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: We had conversations that were identical, there was no difference between our conversations. With all of them, I discussed these orders for placing people into detention, and I insisted on this being done according to the proper procedure. Because sometimes it happened that these orders contained only the name, the signature, and the stamp. There were quite a few cases where, in addition to the full name, there was the date of birth. But, actually, it should also contain such details as the father's name and date of birth, the place of birth, and residential address. So these are the topics that we discussed, but nothing materialised as a result.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And did you have the same sort of conversations with Mr. Zivkovic?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: As I said, I talked about these things with all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Did you discuss the conditions in the prison?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Well, certainly I did mention that in passing. But they were not in a position to accommodate any of my requests.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And what I mean by the conditions in the prison, I'm referring to what you said earlier, in relation to people coming at night and beating prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: Oh, yes, that was common knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And my last question, Mr. Vidic. We've seen all these log-books. We've seen people taken to the hospital, and you've explained to us what these were. Were any of these crimes, to your knowledge, ever processed and tried criminally before a court? Except for the case that you mentioned of the prison guard.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV VIDIC
utterances.text: I know nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Vidic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: In regard to the -- the exhibit numbers, Madam Registrar, could it that be we just gave two exhibit numbers to the same document 1316 and 1317 to -- to 65 ter 3075?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: We have another 15 minutes before the ordinary time for the -- for the adjournment. But I'm wondering whether, on the one hand, counsel may think that little practical use can be made of that. In any event, perhaps the witness could be -- the witness's endurance need not be taxed to squeeze the additional 15 minutes of court time out of today. So perhaps we should take the adjournment to -- Pardon me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Provided, of course, we can finish tomorrow, which is -- I see that counsel requested five hours. Is that still your expectation?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, one thing is certain, we will finish with this witness tomorrow. And our examination will be considerably shorter than our notification, because we always make our notifications in an abundance of caution. But a lot has been already gone through by the Prosecutor. The Prosecutor has also tendered as lot of documents that we intended to introduce, so we will certainly finish by the end of the day tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Vidic, we are about to adjourn for the day. You having been sworn as a witness, you can't have contact with counsel from other side; and should you have occasion to speak with persons outside of the court, you cannot discuss your testimony. Do you understand? So we would -- I think we're in Courtroom III tomorrow morning. So we take the adjournment to 9.00 tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 28th day of April, 2010, at 9.00 a.m. 20 21 22 23 24 25
